issues.issue: Was the Deltaport container terminal a 'project' under CEAA, given construction began before CEAA came into force?
issues.applicant_position: An environmental assessment under section 5 of CEAA was required for the project.
issues.respondent_position: Construction began before CEAA took effect, so there was no 'project' under the Act; the judge was right.
issues.result_quote: We can see no error in this reasoning.

issues.issue: Does the transitional provision (CEAA s. 74) bring the project under CEAA?
issues.applicant_position: No Minister referral occurred, so CEAA applies to the project under the transitional provision.
issues.respondent_position: Section 74 only preserves EARPGO reviews already under way; it does not bring construction projects under CEAA.
issues.result_quote: In our view, the transitional provision of CEAA (s. 74) does not assist the appellant.

issues.issue: Could the Minister have referred the project to a mediator under CEAA s. 48(1) and s. 29?
issues.applicant_position: Section 48(1) allowed a referral to a mediator, and the Minister's refusal was wrong.
issues.result_quote: We, therefore, make no comment on the validity of his submission, on the substance of that section.
